data.name: Manasseh
data.gender_notes: Manasseh is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manasseh is derived from the Hebrew words ‘maná‘ (forgetfulness) and ‘ashi’ (God). This name signifies forgetting God or a person who forgets God's commands or instructions. The name Manasseh carries the meaning “Forgetfulness of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Manasseh usually hope their child will grow to embody forgetfulness of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to stay faithful to God and not forget His teachings and commandments.
data.etymology: Manasseh belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Forgetfulness of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manasseh total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: מנשה
in_hebrew.meaning: שמו של נדבן שפירושו לשכוח או להזכיר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם מנשה הוא שמו של בנו של יוסף, שנולד אחרי שקשה לו לזכור את כל הרעות שעשה לו אחיו. השם נגזר מהמילה העברית 'נשא' שמשמעותה לשכוח, ועל כן השם מנשה מתפרש כ'השוכח' או 'זה שגורם לשכוח'. במסורת היהודית, מנשה היה אחד משנים עשר שבטי ישראל.

in_greek.name: Μανασσης
in_greek.meaning: όνομα που σημαίνει να ξεχνάω ή να θυμίζω
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μανασσης είναι το ελληνικό ισοδύναμο του εβραϊκού ονόματος מנשה. Στη Βίβλο, ο Μανασσης ήταν ο γιος του Ιωσήφ και της Ασηννάθ, και ένας από τους δώδεκα πατριάρχες των Ισραηλινών. Το όνομα Μανασσης προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή λέξη 'נשא', που σημαίνει 'να ξεχνάω', και αναφέρεται στο γεγονός ότι ο Ιωσήφ ξέχασε τις κακοποιίες που του έκαναν οι αδελφοί του.

in_latin.name: Manasseh
in_latin.meaning: name meaning to forget or to cause to forget
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Manasseh is derived from the Hebrew name מנשה, which means 'to forget' or 'causing to forget'. In the Bible, Manasseh was the son of Joseph and Asenath, and one of the twelve patriarchs of the Israelites. The name is significant in Christian tradition as a symbol of redemption and forgiveness.

in_english.name: Manasseh
in_english.long_meaning: The name Manasseh originates from the Hebrew name מנשה, meaning 'to forget' or 'causing to forget'. In the Bible, Manasseh was the son of Joseph and Asenath, and one of the twelve tribes of Israel. The name holds spiritual significance as a symbol of redemption, forgiveness, and new beginnings. It is associated with personality traits such as humility, kindness, and a strong sense of justice. The name Manasseh is used across various Christian cultures, reflecting its enduring significance in biblical tradition.

data.cultural_impact: Manasseh can be found in the Old Testament as the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel and as the name of two kings in the Kingdom of Judah, including a notoriously wicked one who led his nation away from God. Despite this negative association, the name Manasseh has also been used in the English-speaking world as a personal name for centuries, and has produced notable historical figures like the explorer John Manasseh Wallarce and the international soccer star, Manasseh Ishmael Quatshina.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Manasseh may serve as a constant reminder to those who bear it to remember their focus on God, to avoid the pitfalls of forgetting Him, and to strive to live a life in line with His will and instruction. This spiritual significance can be a source of inspiration and motivation, especially in times of doubt or when facing difficult challenges, to remain steadfast in faith and to uphold the values and virtues that are pleasing to God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Manasseh: God has made me forget my troubles. This name was given to the firstborn son of Joseph in the land of Egypt, symbolizing God's grace and mercy in helping the Israelites overcome their hardships.

biblical_reference.note: Manasseh was one of the twelve sons of Jacob, and the ancestor of the tribe of Manasseh.

historical_references.reference: Manasseh was a king of Judah who reigned for 55 years (697-642 BC) and is infamous for leading Judah into idolatry and moral decay. He was the son of Hezekiah and succeeded his father upon Hezekiah's death.
historical_references.context: Ancient Near East, Kingdom of Judah

historical_references.reference: Manasseh is also mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus in the New Testament (Matthew 1:10-11), where he is listed as the father of Amon and the grandfather of Josiah.
historical_references.time_period: Before the birth of Jesus (circa 4 BC)

modern_usage.modern_context: Manasseh is a name with significant historical and biblical roots. It is most commonly recognized from the Old Testament as the name of a king of Judah who ruled during the late 7th century BCE. Manasseh is known for his idolatrous rule and his eventual repentance and restoration. Outside of religious contexts, Manasseh is also the name of a place in modern Israel and a surname found in various countries. In the context of religion and spirituality, the name Manasseh is often associated with the Bible and Jewish and Christian traditions. In the field of history and education, Manasseh is studied as a significant figure in Ancient Near Eastern history and as a contributing factor in the development of the Hebrew Bible. In geography and travel, Manasseh is the name of a mountain range and a settlement in Israel.

name_in_real_life.story: Michael Manasseh from New York, United States embodies the meaning of Manasseh - "Forgetfulness of God". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
